paragraphs.source_en: The old man pointed toward the alcove and urged the master, “Please, do sit over there.” Two or three years earlier the master had thought it made no difference where one sat in a sitting room; but after someone had explained the alcove to him and he had learned that it developed from the raised seat of honor, the place reserved for a lord’s special envoy, he had ever since refused to go anywhere near it. Especially with an elderly stranger planted there so stubbornly, the issue was no longer merely upper seat or lower seat; even a greeting could scarcely be managed. So the master could only make a deep bow.

paragraphs.source_en: “I am honored to make your acquaintance. I hear that Meitei is forever intruding upon your household, and I have long wished to call upon you and profit by your distinguished conversation. As I happened today to be passing near your honored residence, I have taken the liberty of stopping by to express my thanks. Now that I have had the pleasure of meeting you, I beg your continued kindness hereafter!” The old gentleman delivered this old-fashioned greeting with perfect fluency. The master was a man of narrow acquaintance and few words, and having almost never met such an old-fashioned elder, he had felt somewhat out of place from the start and at a loss how to respond; then, showered with this torrent of formal salutations, he completely forgot the Korean ginseng and the red-and-white candy sticks, and could only answer in a strange, flustered voice born of desperation.
